articles.title: Complications After Minimally Invasive vs Open Calcaneal Osteotomy: A Retrospective Study.
articles.authors: Kiriluk SH, Crawford D, Harrison P, Encinas R, O'Keefe J, Davis HT, et al.
articles.population: Patients aged 18 years and over undergoing calcaneal osteotomy for foot deformities
articles.sample_size: 44 open surgery patients, 26 minimally invasive surgery patients
articles.outcomes: Nonunion, nerve complications, wound complications, hardware failure, reoperation, infection, wound dehiscence, pain and function
articles.take_home: Both open and minimally invasive calcaneal osteotomy had similar rates of serious complications and achieved good correction of foot deformities. The minimally invasive approach showed fewer minor wound problems, though this difference was not confirmed as statistically significant after adjustment.

articles.title: A Modified Ponseti Method for Skeletally Mature Complex Foot Deformities.
articles.authors: Zaldivar B, Schuster-Wasserman JA, Caicedo-Gutierrez ML, Cogua-Rodriguez AV, Montoya-Murillo DP, Ortiz-Montoya DF
articles.population: Skeletally mature adolescent and adult patients with idiopathic or acquired complex foot deformities
articles.outcomes: Foot deformity correction, need for additional surgery, plantigrade foot achievement, relapse rates, casting complications, Foot and Ankle Outcome Score
articles.take_home: Using serial casting before surgery (a modified Ponseti method) helped correct complex foot deformities in adults and teenagers, allowing 89% to achieve a properly aligned foot and reducing the need for complex surgery. Most patients had good results with few complications and low relapse rates at follow-up.

articles.title: Incidence and Associated Factors of 2-Legged Nitinol Staple Breakage in Foot and Ankle Surgery.
articles.authors: Ikuta Y, Nakasa T, Ishibashi S, Sakurai S, Moriwaki D, Chujo T, et al.
articles.population: Patients undergoing foot and ankle surgery with 2-legged nitinol staples
articles.outcomes: Nitinol staple breakage rates at minimum 6 months follow-up, assessed on plain radiographs, analysed by anatomical site, implant geometry and fixation strategy
articles.take_home: Overall 4% of nitinol staples broke, with higher breakage rates in certain joints like the calcaneocuboid (22.2%) and talonavicular (12.5%) joints. Using a screw alongside a staple or using symmetric staple designs reduced breakage rates in high-risk areas.

articles.title: Preoperative predictors of arthroscopically confirmed lateral ankle micro-instability and two-year outcomes after arthroscopic repair of the ATFL superior fascicle.
articles.authors: Feng SM, Xue C, Shao CQ, Su CF, Gao SH
articles.study_type: Prospective observational study with surgical cohort follow-up
articles.population: Patients with suspected lateral ankle microinstability
articles.sample_size: 67 patients (45 with confirmed LAM who underwent repair)
articles.outcomes: Anterior talar translation, active joint position sense, AOFAS score, Karlsson Ankle Functional Score at 2 years post-repair
articles.take_home: Combining two simple tests (measuring how far the ankle bone moves forward and how well patients sense ankle position) can accurately predict lateral ankle microinstability before surgery. Arthroscopic repair of the damaged ligament improved ankle stability, position sense, and function over 2 years.

articles.title: What is a symptomatic flexible flatfoot in children? A systematic review on its definition.
articles.authors: De Pellegrin M, Marcucci L, Helmers A, Radler C, Wachowsky M, Lintz F, et al.
articles.outcomes: Definition of symptomatic flexible flatfoot; 15 different symptoms identified including pain, dysfunction, functional impairment, reduced quality of life, altered kinetic chain, daily activity limitation, fatigue, sport limitation, skin lesions, tight Achilles tendon and gait abnormalities; 11 diagnostic tools described
articles.take_home: Symptomatic flexible flatfoot in children involves much more than just pain - it can include dysfunction, difficulty with daily activities, fatigue, sport limitation and other features. Doctors should assess the full picture rather than relying on pain alone.

articles.title: Patient reported outcomes following surgical reconstruction of acquired Charcot foot deformity.
articles.authors: Cho E, Hodkiewicz V, Huang NW, Feffer M, Hamid KS, Schiff AP, et al.
articles.population: Patients with diabetes-associated Charcot foot arthropathy who underwent surgical reconstruction
articles.outcomes: Patient-Reported Outcomes Measurement Information System (PROMIS) Pain Interference, Physical Function, Global Health, and Foot and Ankle Disability Index
articles.take_home: Patients had meaningful improvements in pain and function at 6 months after Charcot foot reconstruction surgery, but these improvements were not sustained at 12 months.

articles.title: Safety and clinical outcomes of transarterial microembolization for accessory navicular syndrome refractory to conservative treatment.
articles.authors: Kubo T, Farhan A, Shibuya M, Miyazaki K, Nakata M, Kawabe A, et al.
articles.population: Patients with accessory navicular syndrome that had not improved with conservative treatment
articles.outcomes: Pain relief measured by Numeric Rating Scale and functional improvement measured by European Foot and Ankle Society scores at 12 months and final follow-up (mean 31 months); safety and adverse events
articles.take_home: Transarterial microembolization was safe and effective for patients with accessory navicular syndrome that had not responded to conservative treatment, with significant improvements in pain and function maintained over nearly 2.5 years on average. No major complications were reported.

articles.title: Radiographic assessment of lesser metatarsophalangeal joint distraction for the diagnosis of plantar plate tears: A cadaveric study.
articles.authors: Chegini-Kord MH, Lal NA, Taseh A, Srinivas S, Bhamidipati A, Avadhuta R, et al.
articles.outcomes: Radiographic joint widening measurements under traction at different forces and dorsiflexion angles; sensitivity and specificity for detecting complete plantar plate tears
articles.take_home: When a specific pulling force is applied to the foot joint, complete tears of the plantar plate ligament cause the joint to widen more than 0.53 cm, which could help doctors diagnose this injury on X-rays. This measurement was 92% accurate at detecting complete tears in this laboratory study.
